item.title: OnRamp Creative Entrepreneur Accelerator: Applications Open — Mon Oct 26, 2:00 PM — Maxwell Hall
item.description:
On-Ramp Creative Entrepreneur Accelerator: Southern Indiana April 19-21, 2027
Pillar Arts and the Indiana University Center for Rural Engagement are partnering with the Indiana Arts Commission to host the On-Ramp Creative Entrepreneur Accelerator for the southern Indiana region. This three-day intensive entrepreneurship and community engagement workshop helps Indiana creative entrepreneurs build a sustainable practice through a portfolio career model. Participants also have the chance to apply for up to $2,000 to put what they learn into action.
The deadline to apply is January 15, 2027, at 4:30 PM ET. An informational webinar will be held November 10, 2026, at 6:00 PM ET. Register for the webinar https://www.zoomgov.com/webinar/register/WN_DBQ7HHY5RAWm5hZV5OVMfQ or learn more and apply https://www.in.gov/arts/programs-and-services/training/on-ramp-creative-entrepreneur-accelerator/ .
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

Baker Professor of Jazz Studies and professor of music in jazz studies at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Oct 27 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Oct 27 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Oct 27 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Oct 30 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Fri Oct 30 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Oct 30, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: We the People — Sun Nov 1, 5:00 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
Join the Bloomington Symphony Orchestra as they perform a concert in recognition of our country’s 250th year. From the familiar square dance feel of Copland’s Hoedown, to the soulful, bluesy tonalities of Still’s Afro-American Symphony, this concert explores what it means to be an American. 4:15pm pre-concert talk 5:00pm performance Program: Aaron Copland – “Hoe-Down” from Rodeo Gary Powell Nash – “In Memoriam Sojourner Truth” Jennifer Higdon – All Things Majestic William Grant Still – Symphony No. 1, “Afro-American” “I travel the world, and I’m happy to say that America is still the great melting pot – maybe a chunky stew rather than a melting pot at this point, but you know what I mean.” – Philip Glass, 1999 NPR interview BSO Season Passes can be purchased until October 16th. Passes include discounted tickets to all 4 season concerts, reserved seating, and other benefits. To learn more and purchase your Season Pass, visit bloomingtonsymphony.com/seasonpass57

item.title: Embedded Counseling (CAPS) — Mon Nov 2, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
Supporting your well-being is an important part of our work at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. That's why we are proud to partner with Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS) to provide an embedded counselor in our space every Monday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mollibeth Penner, LHMCA serves as our embedded counselor and works directly with students connected to the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. To schedule an appointment, please call CAPS (https://healthcenter.indiana.edu/make-appointment/index.html) and let them know you are an LGBTQ+ Culture Center student interested in meeting with Mollibeth at the center. We hope this partnership makes it easier for you to access support in a space where you feel comfortable and affirmed. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.
Source: IU LGBTQ+ Culture Center

item.title: Fall Color Hike: Lake Strahl, Brown County State Park — Mon Nov 2, 11:00 AM — Brown County State Park
item.description:
Join a park naturalist for a guided hike of Trail 6 around Lake Strahl! Hear about the history of the lake, the surrounding Strahl Valley, and learn about the animals that make it their home, all while enjoying beautiful fall colors. The section of Trail 6 around Lake Strahl is considered easy to moderate. It has some short staircases, uneven surfaces, tree roots, and possible wet spots. The trail is less than a mile and will take about 45 minutes to complete. Meet at the Lake Strahl parking lot.
Source: Brown County State Park
